---
title: "Epidemiology and Disease Surveillance Unit — Ministry of Health, Zambia"
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%B %d, %Y')`"
output:
  pdf_document:
    latex_engine: xelatex
    fig_caption: true
  officedown::rdocx_document:
    reference_docx: null
    tables:
      style: Table Grid
      layout: autofit
      width: 1.0
    plots:
      style: Normal
      align: center
params:
  week_number:  34
  week_start:   "19th August 2024"
  week_end:     "25th August 2024"
  year:         2024
  run_python:   true
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SETUP
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo      = FALSE,
  message   = FALSE,
  warning   = FALSE,
  dpi       = 150,
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "100%"
)

# ── Packages ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
required_packages <- c(
  "tidyverse", "readxl", "knitr", "flextable",
  "officer", "officedown", "scales", "here", "sf", "patchwork"
)
for (pkg in required_packages) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages(pkg, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org", quiet = TRUE)
  suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(pkg, character.only = TRUE))
}

# ── Paths ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
root_dir    <- here::here()
data_dir    <- file.path(root_dir, "data")
figures_dir <- file.path(root_dir, "outputs")

# ──  summary table PNG only ───────────────────────────────────────────
# All charts and the choropleth map are rendered natively in R (see functions
# below). Python is only called to produce summary_table.png.
if (params$run_python) {
  py_script <- file.path(root_dir, "scripts", "generate_plots.py")
  if (file.exists(py_script))
    system2("python3", py_script, stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE)
}

# ── Load surveillance CSVs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
weekly  <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "weekly_data_by_province.csv"),
                    show_col_types = FALSE)
msl     <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "measles_lab.csv"),
                    show_col_types = FALSE)

# ── Derived summaries ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
wk34 <- weekly %>% filter(week == params$week_number, year == params$year)

# Helper: "Province(N), ..." string from rows where col > 0
prov_bullet <- function(df, col) {
  df %>%
    filter(.data[[col]] > 0) %>%
    arrange(province) %>%
    mutate(lbl = paste0(province, "(", .data[[col]], ")")) %>%
    pull(lbl) %>% paste(collapse = ", ")
}

afp_prov     <- prov_bullet(wk34, "afp_suspected")
anthrax_prov <- prov_bullet(wk34, "anthrax_suspected")
cholera_prov <- prov_bullet(wk34, "cholera_suspected")
measles_prov <- prov_bullet(wk34, "measles_suspected")
malaria_prov <- prov_bullet(wk34, "malaria_suspected")
diarr_prov   <- prov_bullet(wk34, "non_bloody_diarrhoea_suspected")
typhoid_prov <- prov_bullet(wk34, "typhoid_suspected")

afp_tot     <- sum(wk34$afp_suspected)
anthrax_tot <- sum(wk34$anthrax_suspected)
cholera_tot <- sum(wk34$cholera_suspected)
measles_tot <- sum(wk34$measles_suspected)
malaria_tot <- sum(wk34$malaria_suspected)
diarr_tot   <- sum(wk34$non_bloody_diarrhoea_suspected)
typhoid_tot <- sum(wk34$typhoid_suspected)

ml_suspected <- sum(msl$total_suspected)
ml_tested    <- sum(msl$specimens_tested)
ml_positive  <- sum(msl$positive)
ml_pr        <- round(ml_positive / ml_tested * 100, 1)

fmt <- function(x) scales::comma(x)

# ── Priority disease summary table ────────────────────────────────────────────
summary_data <- tibble(
  `Disease/Event/Condition` = c(
    "AFP", "Anthrax", "Cholera", "Non-bloody Diarrhoea",
    "Malaria", "Measles", "Monkeypox", "Plague", "Typhoid Fever"),
  Sus34  = c(6,    8,     4,      35175,   144640, 28, 0,  0,  33),
  Tes34  = c(4,    2,     0,       2435,   138717, 21, 0,  0,  20),
  Con34  = c(1,    1,     0,       2171,    40329,  3, 0,  0,   4),
  SusCum = c(318,  283, 16684,   813029, 8011914, 4360, 8, 13, 822),
  TesCum = c(259,   36,  4410,    46953, 7570205, 1343, 4,  1, 499),
  ConCum = c(1,     5,   2034,    50502, 3693242,  655, 0,  0,  45)
) %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), fmt))

# ── Maternal deaths summary stats ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Defined here in setup so mat_wk_n and mat_cum are available to the
# maternal-panel chunk (which runs before maternal-bullets).
raw_mat_setup <- read_csv(
  file.path(data_dir, "maternal_deaths.csv"),
  col_names = FALSE, show_col_types = FALSE
)
prov_rows_setup <- raw_mat_setup %>%
  set_names(c("province", "deaths_cum", "week34_col")) %>%
  filter(province != "province", province != "cause") %>%
  mutate(deaths_cum = as.integer(deaths_cum))

mat_cum  <- sum(prov_rows_setup$deaths_cum)
mat_wk_n <- 15   # total weekly maternal deaths (from bulletin)
```

```{r fn-measles-lab, include=FALSE}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# FUNCTION: plot_measles_lab()
#
# Produces the "Measles Laboratory Test Results by Province" stacked bar chart.
#
# Data:    data/measles_lab.csv
#          Columns: province, positive, negative, indeterminate, pending,
#                   not_done, total_suspected, specimens_tested
#
# Steps:
#   1. Read measles_lab.csv
#   2. Select the five result columns and pivot wide → long (one row per
#      province × result category)
#   3. Apply ordered factors so the x-axis follows PROVINCE_ORDER and the
#      stack follows RESULT_ORDER (bottom → top)
#   4. geom_col with position_stack draws filled stacked bars
#   5. scale_fill_manual maps each result category to its exact hex colour
#   6. theme_classic + custom tweaks replicates the bulletin style
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ── Colour palette ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
RESULT_COLOURS <- c(
  "Indeterminate" = "#4a7c59",   # muted green
  "Negative"      = "#457b9d",   # steel blue
  "Not done"      = "#adb5bd",   # light grey
  "Pending"       = "#6d2b9e",   # purple
  "Positive"      = "#e63946"    # red
)

# Stack order bottom → top; also controls legend order
RESULT_ORDER <- c("Indeterminate", "Negative", "Not done", "Pending", "Positive")

# X-axis province sequence
PROVINCE_ORDER <- c(
  "Central", "Copperbelt", "Eastern", "Luapula", "Lusaka",
  "Muchinga", "North-Western", "Northern", "Southern", "Western"
)

plot_measles_lab <- function(
    df        = NULL,                                    # optional pre-loaded df
    save_path = here("outputs", "measles_lab_bar.png"), # NULL → no file saved
    width_in  = 7.5,
    height_in = 3.8,
    dpi       = 150
) {

  # Step 1 — load data
  if (is.null(df))
    df <- read_csv(here("data", "measles_lab.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

  # Step 2 — pivot wide → long
  df_long <- df %>%
    select(province, positive, negative, indeterminate, pending, not_done) %>%
    rename(
      Positive      = positive,
      Negative      = negative,
      Indeterminate = indeterminate,
      Pending       = pending,
      `Not done`    = not_done
    ) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols      = -province,
      names_to  = "result",
      values_to = "count"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      province = factor(province, levels = PROVINCE_ORDER),
      result   = factor(result,   levels = RESULT_ORDER)
    )

  # Step 3 — build ggplot
  p <- ggplot(df_long, aes(x = province, y = count, fill = result)) +

    # Stacked bars with white segment gaps
    geom_col(
      position  = position_stack(reverse = FALSE),
      width     = 0.6,
      colour    = "white",
      linewidth = 0.3
    ) +

    # Exact bulletin colours per result category
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = RESULT_COLOURS,
      breaks = RESULT_ORDER,
      name   = "Result"
    ) +

    # Uppercase province labels on x axis
    scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) str_to_upper(x)) +

    # Y axis: integer breaks, no gap below 0
    scale_y_continuous(
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05)),
      breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 5)
    ) +

    labs(x = NULL, y = "Number of specimens") +

    theme_classic(base_size = 10, base_family = "sans") +
    theme(
      axis.text.x          = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1,
                                           size = 7.5, colour = "#333333"),
      axis.text.y          = element_text(size = 8,   colour = "#555555"),
      axis.title.y         = element_text(size = 9,   colour = "#444444"),
      axis.line.x          = element_line(colour = "#cccccc"),
      axis.line.y          = element_line(colour = "#cccccc"),
      axis.ticks           = element_line(colour = "#cccccc"),
      legend.title         = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
      legend.text          = element_text(size = 8),
      legend.key.size      = unit(0.4, "cm"),
      legend.position      = "right",
      legend.justification = "top",
      panel.grid           = element_blank(),
      panel.background     = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      plot.background      = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      plot.margin          = margin(4, 6, 4, 4, unit = "pt")
    )

  # Step 4 — save
  if (!is.null(save_path)) {
    dir.create(dirname(save_path), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
    ggsave(save_path, plot = p, width = width_in, height = height_in,
           dpi = dpi, bg = "white")
    return(invisible(p))
  }

  return(p)
}
```

```{r fn-maternal-causes, include=FALSE}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# FUNCTION: plot_maternal_causes()
#
# Produces the "Causes of maternal death (Week 34, n=15)" horizontal bar chart.
#
# Data:    data/maternal_deaths.csv
#          The CSV holds two logical tables in one file:
#            Rows 1–10  → province cumulative deaths
#            Row  11    → embedded header: "cause, deaths_week34, percent"
#            Rows 12–16 → five cause rows
#          Parsing: read with col_names = FALSE, locate the embedded "cause"
#          header row by value, slice the rows below it.
#
# Steps:
#   1. Read raw CSV without header inference
#   2. Find the row where column 1 == "cause" (the embedded header)
#   3. Slice rows below it, assign names, cast to integer
#   4. Apply rev(CAUSE_ORDER) as factor levels so the longest bar sits at the
#      top (ggplot draws y-axis factors bottom → top, so rev() is required)
#   5. geom_col draws horizontal bars; geom_text adds % labels to the right
#   6. scale_x_continuous with 25 % right expansion prevents label clipping
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Teal bar colour matching the bulletin
MAT_BAR_COLOUR <- "#2a9d8f"

# Desired display order: longest bar at top → shortest at bottom
CAUSE_ORDER <- c(
  "Obstetric haemorrhage",
  "Non-obstetric complications",
  "Unanticipated complications",
  "Hypertensive disorder",
  "Pregnancy-related infection"
)

plot_maternal_causes <- function(
    df        = NULL,                                       # optional pre-loaded df
    save_path = here("outputs", "maternal_causes_bar.png"), # NULL → no file saved
    width_in  = 5.2,
    height_in = 3.2,
    dpi       = 150
) {

  # Step 1-3 — load and parse data
  if (is.null(df)) {
    raw <- read_csv(
      here("data", "maternal_deaths.csv"),
      col_names      = FALSE,
      show_col_types = FALSE
    )

    # Row where the first column equals the literal string "cause"
    header_row <- which(raw[[1]] == "cause")

    df <- raw[(header_row + 1):nrow(raw), 1:3] %>%
      set_names(c("cause", "deaths_week34", "percent")) %>%
      mutate(
        deaths_week34 = as.integer(deaths_week34),
        percent       = as.integer(percent)
      )
  }

  # Step 4 — ordered factor: rev() places longest bar at the top
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(cause = factor(cause, levels = rev(CAUSE_ORDER)))

  # Step 5 — build ggplot
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = deaths_week34, y = cause)) +

    # Horizontal filled bars
    geom_col(
      fill      = MAT_BAR_COLOUR,
      width     = 0.55,
      colour    = "white",
      linewidth = 0.3
    ) +

    # Percentage labels just to the right of each bar
    geom_text(
      aes(label = paste0(percent, "%")),
      hjust  = -0.15,
      vjust  = 0.5,
      size   = 3.2,
      colour = "#333333"
    ) +

    # Step 6 — 25 % right padding keeps labels inside the plot area
    scale_x_continuous(
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25)),
      breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 4)
    ) +

    labs(x = "# of maternal deaths", y = NULL) +

    theme_classic(base_size = 10, base_family = "sans") +
    theme(
      axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 8,   colour = "#555555"),
      axis.text.y      = element_text(size = 8.5, colour = "#333333",
                                      hjust = 1),
      axis.title.x     = element_text(size = 9,   colour = "#444444"),
      axis.line.x      = element_line(colour = "#cccccc"),
      axis.line.y      = element_line(colour = "#cccccc"),
      axis.ticks       = element_line(colour = "#cccccc"),
      panel.grid       = element_blank(),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      plot.margin      = margin(4, 10, 4, 4, unit = "pt")
    )

  # Save
  if (!is.null(save_path)) {
    dir.create(dirname(save_path), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
    ggsave(save_path, plot = p, width = width_in, height = height_in,
           dpi = dpi, bg = "white")
    return(invisible(p))
  }
  return(p)
}
```

```{r fn-maternal-map, include=FALSE}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# FUNCTION: plot_maternal_map()
#
# Produces the "Cumulative distribution of maternal deaths (2024) by province"
# choropleth map.
#
# Data:    data/maternal_deaths.csv  (province rows — same file as above)
#          Zambia_-_Administrative_District_Boundaries_2022.shp
#          (116 districts, EPSG:3857)
#
# Three-layer rendering strategy (replicates the sample bulletin exactly):
#   Layer 1 — Province fills   : BuPu choropleth. Districts are dissolved to
#                                 province polygons via st_union(); each
#                                 province is filled by its deaths count.
#   Layer 2 — District borders : thin #aaaaaa lines drawn over the fills,
#                                 making internal district sub-divisions
#                                 visible within each province.
#   Layer 3 — Province borders : thick #444444 lines redrawn on top, giving
#                                 each province a clearly defined outer edge.
#
# Label connectors:
#   - st_centroid() computes the geographic centre of each province polygon.
#   - geom_segment() draws a line from centroid to a manually calibrated
#     label position (LABEL_POS) that matches the sample bulletin layout.
#   - geom_label() places "Province(N)" text with a white background box.
#
# Shapefiles searched in order:
#   1. /mnt/user-data/uploads/Zambia_-_Administrative_District_Boundaries_2022.shp
#   2. data/Zambia_-_Administrative_District_Boundaries_2022.shp
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Shapefile search paths
DIST_SHP_PATHS <- c(
  here("data","shape files","Zambia_-_Administrative_District_Boundaries_2022.shp"),
  here("data","shape files", "Zambia_-_Administrative_District_Boundaries_2022.shp")
)

# BuPu palette matches the sample bulletin
MAP_PALETTE <- "BuPu"

# Label positions calibrated to the sample bulletin (WGS84 decimal degrees).
# Province centroids are computed from the shapefile; label anchors are placed
# outside the province to avoid overlap, with connector lines joining them.
#   Centroids for reference:
#     Central(28.24,-14.41)  Copperbelt(27.85,-13.12)  Eastern(31.90,-13.58)
#     Luapula(29.21,-10.67)  Lusaka(29.08,-15.43)       Muchinga(31.97,-11.33)
#     North-Western(25.05,-13.03)  Northern(30.65,-9.72)
#     Southern(26.76,-16.79)       Western(23.68,-15.64)
LABEL_POS <- tribble(
  ~province,         ~lx,    ~ly,
  "Northern",        32.9,   -8.85,
  "Luapula",         32.3,  -10.15,
  "Muchinga",        33.6,  -11.15,
  "Eastern",         33.65, -13.70,
  "Central",         29.5,  -14.05,
  "Copperbelt",      28.2,  -14.20,
  "Lusaka",          31.0,  -15.85,
  "North-Western",   22.3,  -12.20,
  "Western",         21.7,  -15.60,
  "Southern",        27.1,  -17.85
)

plot_maternal_map <- function(
    deaths_df = NULL,                                        # optional pre-loaded df
    save_path = here("outputs", "maternal_deaths_map.png"), # NULL → no file saved
    width_in  = 6.2,
    height_in = 5.8,
    dpi       = 180
) {

  # Step 1 — load and parse province deaths data
  if (is.null(deaths_df)) {
    raw <- read_csv(
      here("data", "maternal_deaths.csv"),
      col_names      = FALSE,
      show_col_types = FALSE
    )
    # Skip both embedded headers; keep only the 10 province data rows
    deaths_df <- raw %>%
      set_names(c("province", "maternal_deaths_cumulative", "week34")) %>%
      filter(
        province != "province",  # skip the first header row stored as data
        province != "cause"      # skip the embedded second-table header
      ) %>%
      select(province, maternal_deaths = maternal_deaths_cumulative) %>%
      mutate(maternal_deaths = as.integer(maternal_deaths))
  }

  # Step 2 — load district shapefile, reproject to WGS84
  shp_path <- NULL
  for (p in DIST_SHP_PATHS) {
    if (file.exists(p)) { shp_path <- p; break }
  }
  if (is.null(shp_path))
    stop("Shapefile 'Zambia_-_Administrative_District_Boundaries_2022.shp' ",
         "not found in /mnt/user-data/uploads/ or data/")

  districts <- st_read(shp_path, quiet = TRUE) %>%
    st_transform(4326)

  # Dissolve 116 district polygons → 10 province polygons
  provinces <- districts %>%
    group_by(PROVINCE) %>%
    summarise(geometry = st_union(geometry), .groups = "drop") %>%
    rename(province = PROVINCE) %>%
    left_join(deaths_df, by = "province")   # attach deaths counts

  # Step 3 — compute province centroids for connector-line origins
  centroids <- provinces %>%
    st_centroid() %>%
    mutate(
      cx = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1],
      cy = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2]
    ) %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    select(province, cx, cy)

  labels <- LABEL_POS %>%
    left_join(centroids, by = "province") %>%
    left_join(deaths_df, by = "province")

  # Step 4 — build ggplot (three layers + labels)
  p <- ggplot() +

    # Layer 1: province choropleth fill (no borders yet)
    geom_sf(
      data   = provinces,
      aes(fill = maternal_deaths),
      colour = NA
    ) +

    # BuPu continuous scale, range 18–65, ticks at 20 / 40 / 60
    scale_fill_distiller(
      palette   = MAP_PALETTE,
      direction = 1,
      limits    = c(18, 65),
      breaks    = c(20, 40, 60),
      name      = "Cumulative\nMaternal Deaths",
      guide     = guide_colorbar(
        direction      = "horizontal",
        title.position = "top",
        barwidth       = unit(3.5, "cm"),
        barheight      = unit(0.35, "cm"),
        ticks          = TRUE
      )
    ) +

    # Layer 2: thin district lines → sub-divisions visible inside provinces
    geom_sf(data = districts, fill = NA,
            colour = "#aaaaaa", linewidth = 0.2) +

    # Layer 3: thick province borders → clearly defined outer boundaries
    geom_sf(data = provinces, fill = NA,
            colour = "#444444", linewidth = 0.8) +

    # Connector lines: centroid → label anchor
    geom_segment(
      data      = labels,
      aes(x = cx, y = cy, xend = lx, yend = ly),
      colour    = "#444444",
      linewidth = 0.4
    ) +

    # Dots at province centroids
    geom_point(
      data   = labels,
      aes(x = cx, y = cy),
      size   = 1.5,
      colour = "#222222"
    ) +

    # Province labels with white background
    geom_label(
      data          = labels,
      aes(x = lx, y = ly,
          label = paste0(province, "(", maternal_deaths, ")")),
      size          = 2.4,
      colour        = "#111111",
      fill          = "white",
      label.size    = NA,
      label.padding = unit(0.12, "lines"),
      fontface      = "plain"
    ) +

    theme_void(base_family = "sans") +
    theme(
      legend.position      = c(0.18, 0.97),
      legend.justification = c(0.5, 1),
      legend.title         = element_text(size = 6.5, colour = "#333333"),
      legend.text          = element_text(size = 6,   colour = "#333333"),
      plot.background      = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      plot.margin          = margin(2, 2, 2, 2, unit = "pt")
    ) +

    coord_sf(expand = FALSE)

  # Save
  if (!is.null(save_path)) {
    dir.create(dirname(save_path), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
    ggsave(save_path, plot = p, width = width_in, height = height_in,
           dpi = dpi, bg = "white")
    return(invisible(p))
  }
  return(p)
}
```

```{r fn-headlines, include=FALSE}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# HEADLINE BANNER FUNCTIONS
#
# Three functions, one per banner style in the sample bulletin.
# Colour codes are used directly — no intermediate constants.
#
#  banner_main()    — background "#2d6a4f" (dark green),  centred white bold
#                     Used for: main title, "Summary of VPD...", "Maternal Deaths"
#
#  banner_section() — background "#52b788" (medium green), left-aligned white bold
#                     Used for: "Summary", "Summary Report Priority Diseases..."
#
#  banner_sub()     — background "#e07b39" (orange),      centred white bold
#                     Used for: "Measles Laboratory Test Results by Province",
#                               "Causes of maternal death (Week 34, n=15)",
#                               "Cumulative distribution of maternal deaths..."
#
# Each function returns a ggplot object rendered as a narrow coloured strip.
# ggplot2::annotate("rect") fills the panel with the hex colour.
# ggplot2::annotate("text") places bold white text over it.
# theme_void() removes all axes, gridlines, and backgrounds.
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

#' Dark-green banner (#2d6a4f) — main title and major section headings
#' @param label  text string to display
#' @param size   font size in ggplot units (default 4.2 ≈ 12 pt)
banner_main <- function(label, size = 4.2) {
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::annotate("rect",
      xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
      fill = "#2d6a4f"                       # dark green
    ) +
    ggplot2::annotate("text",
      x = 0.5, y = 0.5,
      label    = label,
      colour   = "white",
      fontface = "bold",
      size     = size,
      hjust    = 0.5,
      vjust    = 0.5
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    ggplot2::theme_void() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.margin     = ggplot2::margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
      plot.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "#2d6a4f", colour = NA)
    )
}

#' Medium-green banner (#52b788) — sub-section headings, left-aligned
#' @param label  text string to display
#' @param size   font size in ggplot units (default 3.8 ≈ 11 pt)
banner_section <- function(label, size = 3.8) {
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::annotate("rect",
      xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
      fill = "#52b788"                       # medium green
    ) +
    ggplot2::annotate("text",
      x = 0.01, y = 0.5,
      label    = label,
      colour   = "white",
      fontface = "bold",
      size     = size,
      hjust    = 0,                          # left-aligned
      vjust    = 0.5
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    ggplot2::theme_void() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.margin     = ggplot2::margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
      plot.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "#52b788", colour = NA)
    )
}

#' Orange banner (#e07b39) — figure and chart headers, centred
#' @param label  text string to display
#' @param size   font size in ggplot units (default 3.2 ≈ 9 pt)
banner_sub <- function(label, size = 3.2) {
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::annotate("rect",
      xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
      fill = "#e07b39"                       # orange
    ) +
    ggplot2::annotate("text",
      x = 0.5, y = 0.5,
      label    = label,
      colour   = "white",
      fontface = "bold",
      size     = size,
      hjust    = 0.5,
      vjust    = 0.5
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    ggplot2::theme_void() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.margin     = ggplot2::margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
      plot.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "#e07b39", colour = NA)
    )
}

#' Lime-green banner (#92D050) — section headings matching the sample bulletin:
#' "Summary", "Summary Report Priority Diseases...",
#' "Summary of VPD Surveillance Indicators", "Maternal Deaths"
#' @param label  text string to display
#' @param size   font size in ggplot units (default 4.2 ≈ 12 pt)
banner_green <- function(label, size = 4.2) {
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::annotate("rect",
      xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
      fill = "#92D050"                       # lime green — sample bulletin colour
    ) +
    ggplot2::annotate("text",
      x = 0.5, y = 0.5,
      label    = label,
      colour   = "white",
      fontface = "bold",
      size     = size,
      hjust    = 0.5,
      vjust    = 0.5
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    ggplot2::theme_void() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.margin     = ggplot2::margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
      plot.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "#92D050", colour = NA)
    )
}
```

```{r fn-side-by-side, include=FALSE}
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# FUNCTION: plot_maternal_panel()
#
# Places "Causes of maternal death" and "Cumulative distribution of maternal
# deaths by province" side by side with their orange sub-banners above each,
# exactly as in the sample bulletin.
#
# Strategy:
#   Uses the patchwork package to combine four ggplot objects in a 2×2 grid:
#     [banner_causes]  [banner_map  ]   ← row 1: orange sub-banners
#     [p_causes      ] [p_map       ]   ← row 2: the two charts
#
#   patchwork::plot_layout() controls:
#     heights = c(0.08, 1)  — banner row is ~8% of total height
#     widths  = c(1, 1)     — equal column widths
#
# @param p_causes  ggplot from plot_maternal_causes()
# @param p_map     ggplot from plot_maternal_map()
# @param week      week number for the causes banner label
# @param n         total deaths for the causes banner label
# @return          a patchwork object (print() renders it)
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

plot_maternal_panel <- function(
    p_causes,
    p_map,
    week = 34,
    n    = 15
) {
  # Build the two orange sub-banners dynamically
  b_causes <- banner_sub(
    paste0("Causes of maternal death (Week ", week, ", n=", n, ")")
  )
  b_map <- banner_sub(
    "Cumulative distribution of maternal deaths (2024) by province"
  )

  # Combine: banners on top, charts below, side by side.
  # patchwork: | = horizontal, / = vertical stack
  combined <- (b_causes | b_map) /
              (p_causes  | p_map) +
    patchwork::plot_layout(
      heights = c(0.08, 1),
      widths  = c(1, 1)
    )

  return(combined)
}
```

flextable(summary_data) %>%
  set_header_labels(
    `Disease/Event/Condition` = "Disease/Event/Condition",
    Sus34  = "Suspected",
    Tes34  = "Tested",
    Con34  = "Confirmed",
    SusCum = "Suspected",
    TesCum = "Tested",
    ConCum = "Confirmed"
  ) %>%
  add_header_row(
    values    = c(
      "",
      "Week 34",
      "Week 1 to 34, Cumulative Total"
    ),
    colwidths = c(1, 3, 3)
  ) %>%
  bg(i = 1, part = "header", bg = "#e07b39") %>%   # orange — outer header row
  color(i = 1, part = "header", color = "white") %>%
  bold(i = 1, part = "header") %>%
  bg(i = 2, part = "header", bg = "#f4a261") %>%   # light orange — inner header row
  color(i = 2, part = "header", color = "white") %>%
  bold(i = 2, part = "header") %>%
  bg(i = seq(1, nrow(summary_data), 2), part = "body", bg = "#f7f9f4") %>%
  bg(i = seq(2, nrow(summary_data), 2), part = "body", bg = "white") %>%
  align(j = 2:7, align = "center", part = "all") %>%
  align(j = 1,   align = "left",   part = "all") %>%
  width(j = 1, width = 2.0) %>%
  width(j = 2:7, width = 0.82) %>%
  fontsize(size = 9, part = "all") %>%
  font(fontname = "Calibri", part = "all") %>%
  border_outer(border = fp_border(color = "#aaaaaa", width = 0.5)) %>%
  hline(border = fp_border(color = "#dddddd", width = 0.3), part = "body") %>%
  set_table_properties(layout = "autofit", width = 1)
